post_title: What will the IEA's November 2026 Oil Market Report say about the change in world oil demand in 2026 (y/y, mb/d)?

question.title: What will the IEA's November 2026 Oil Market Report say about the change in world oil demand in 2026 (y/y, mb/d)?
question.description:
The IEA's monthly Oil Market Report (OMR) is the benchmark public data-and-forecast product for global oil supply, demand, stocks, prices and refining activity. It is released at 10:00 Paris time on its scheduled day; the November 2026 edition is scheduled for 13 November 2026, and the October 2026 edition was published on 14 October 2026.

Status quo: in the October 2026 OMR the IEA put 2026 world oil demand at 102.4 mb/d, a fall of 2.6 mb/d year-on-year, with demand in 4Q26 down 2.5 mb/d y/y. It also projected a partial 2 mb/d recovery in 2027 that would still leave global oil use 620 kb/d (0.6%) below 2025 levels. The downgrade path has been steep and persistent within 2026: 2026 demand growth was put at -1.1 mb/d in the June 2026 OMR, -1.0 mb/d in July, -1.6 mb/d in August (941 kb/d steeper than the July assessment), -2.5 mb/d in September and -2.6 mb/d in October. The driver is the US–Iran war and the near-closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which the IEA describes as manifesting itself through restricted product availability, soaring fuel prices and a deteriorating economic outlook; diesel accounts for roughly 25% of the demand loss. In September 2026, North Sea Dated crude averaged USD 116.89/bbl, global oil supply rose 2.5 mb/d m-o-m to 102.3 mb/d, observed global inventories fell by 10 mb, and October refinery runs were forecast at 81.3 mb/d.

For comparison, in the IEF's October 2026 cross-agency analysis OPEC put 2026 demand at 105.7 mb/d (+0.2 mb/d y/y) and the EIA at 102.4 mb/d (-2.0 mb/d), versus the IEA's 102.4 mb/d (-2.6 mb/d) — a 2.2 mb/d spread in 2026 growth estimates, illustrating how much genuine uncertainty surrounds the current level of demand.

Forecasting considerations: outside crises the IEA typically revises its annual demand growth figure by 0.1–0.3 mb/d from one monthly edition to the next, but in 2026 revisions have reached roughly 0.9 mb/d in a single month. The November 2026 edition will fold in newly available monthly demand data for September/October 2026 and the latest developments on the Iran war, Strait of Hormuz shipping, product prices and refining — analysis of those factors, and of the direction of recent revisions, is what should drive a forecast.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the 2026 year-on-year change in world oil demand as reported in the IEA's [Oil Market Report – November 2026](https://www.iea.org/reports/oil-market-report-november-2026), scheduled for publication at 10:00 Paris time on 13 November 2026. The governing figure is the full-year 2026 annual-average y/y change stated in that report's demand overview/highlights, which the OMR gives in million barrels per day to one decimal place — for example, if it states that world oil demand falls by 2.7 mb/d on average in 2026, the question resolves as -2.7, and a stated rise of 0.4 mb/d resolves as 0.4. If the overview states the figure only in thousands of barrels per day, it is converted by dividing by 1,000 (e.g. -2,650 kb/d resolves as -2.65). The figure as first published in the November 2026 edition governs; later revisions (for example in the December 2026 OMR or in IEA databases) do not affect resolution, and if publication is delayed beyond 13 November 2026 the question resolves once that edition is published.
question.fine_print: The figure refers to the IEA's own global oil demand series for total liquids for calendar year 2026 as a whole (full-year annual average), not to a quarterly figure and not to another institution's estimate. If the IEA's November 2026 report page is unavailable or the figure cannot be read from it, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the figure from the IEA's November 2026 OMR will be used.
